per_depth.common_affordance: The guarantee that exactly one certificate category applies, allowing a JOB result to be selected without comparing it against machine-load certificates.
The promise that an input cannot contain both an individual-job witness and a machine-load witness, allowing every solution to prioritize JOB without handling overlaps.
The statement explicitly makes the complete rejection decision equivalent to checking one per-job sum and two aggregate machine sums, with exactly one applicable case guaranteed.
The certificate scenarios reduce infeasibility to additive lower bounds: p1 + p2 for one job and the total load on one machine.
The certificate predicates are explicit strict-greater-than comparisons against T, so equality is treated as non-rejection.
The statement directly exposes complete local and aggregate feasibility inequalities that can be checked independently, eliminating any need to reason about the two-stage pipeline.

The statement makes both certificate categories reducible to independent arithmetic: an isolated job has completion time `p1 + p2`, while continuous machine utilization has duration equal to the sum of that machine's processing times.
The certificate transformations zero all irrelevant processing times, causing the given flow-shop recurrences to collapse to the isolated-job sum p1[i]+p2[i] or a single-machine total sum.
The zeroed-out hypothetical sequences make every certificate value a direct closed form: p1[i] + p2[i] for JOB i, sum(p1) for LOAD 1, or sum(p2) for LOAD 2.
The explicitly zeroed hypothetical simulations, whose recurrence reduces an isolated job to p1_i+p2_i and a saturated machine to a sum of processing times.
